plan_sources.what_you_get: Whatever drawing set the owner kept: permit or record (as-built) drawings, often as PDF; for a building with an existing ERCES, its approved plans and acceptance test report.
plan_sources.how: Written request to the property manager naming the sheets you need (see plan_request). Ask the owner to authorize the architect or GC to release CAD/BIM files directly to you.
plan_sources.limits: Owners often hold only PDFs or paper. Copyright in the design stays with the architect: an architectural work includes the building design as embodied in plans or drawings.

plan_sources.what_you_get: The current construction set (permit drawings plus revisions), and coordination models if the project uses BIM.
plan_sources.how: Submit a Request for Information through the GC; AIA G716 is the standard form any party (owner, architect, contractor) uses to request information from another during construction. Number and log each RFI.
plan_sources.limits: An RFI response is not authorization for extra work; the GC may need the architect's or owner's permission before sharing CAD backgrounds.

plan_sources.what_you_get: CAD backgrounds (DWG/DXF) or the BIM model (Revit, exportable to IFC); wall-type, partition and glazing schedules; life-safety/code plans.
plan_sources.how: Request through the owner or GC with the owner's written authorization; expect the architect to ask for a file-release agreement.
plan_sources.limits: Drawings are instruments of professional service; California building departments cannot duplicate stamped plans without the design professional's and owner's written permission.

plan_sources.source: MEP / electrical / fire alarm engineer and low-voltage contractor
plan_sources.what_you_get: Electrical and fire alarm riser diagrams, electrical/IDF room locations, pathways and firestop details; the fire alarm interface the ERCES must report to.
plan_sources.how: Request through the GC or owner alongside the architectural set.
plan_sources.limits: Same release restrictions as the architectural set.

plan_sources.source: City/county permit portal (Accela Citizen Access, Tyler EnerGov CSS, CentralSquare eTRAKiT, OpenGov)
plan_sources.what_you_get: Permit records by address or number: status, type, dates, inspections, sometimes attachments (plan sheets, approved documents).
plan_sources.how: Search the jurisdiction's public portal by address or permit number. EnerGov CSS and OpenGov allow searching public records without logging in; Accela General Search shows processing status.
plan_sources.limits: Attachments are often restricted: Arapahoe's Accela portal needs the case manager to grant access to download secure documents; Johnstown's eTRAKiT requires login to view attachments and older records need a records request; OpenGov shows only record types the agency enabled for public search.

plan_sources.source: Public-records request to the building department (state open-records law)
plan_sources.what_you_get: Inspection, and sometimes copies, of the official plan set on file.
plan_sources.how: File under the state's public-records law with the city clerk or building department. Federal FOIA covers federal agency records, not city permit files.
plan_sources.limits: Florida exempts building plans of agency-owned structures and of many private facility types (offices, retail, hotels, health care, industrial) held by an agency, and exempts security/firesafety system plans. California allows inspection only; copies need the designer's and owner's written permission (or a court order) plus a signed affidavit limiting use to maintenance, operation and use of the building.

plan_sources.what_you_get: Fire department pre-plans covering building construction, access and hazards.
plan_sources.how: Ask the AHJ's fire prevention office; pre-incident planning now sits in NFPA 1660 (2024), which consolidated NFPA 1620.
plan_sources.limits: Internal fire-department documents; Florida exempts security and firesafety system plans of private property held by an agency from public disclosure.

plan_sources.source: Open building data (OSM, Microsoft, Overture, FEMA USA Structures, USACE NSI, assessor parcels)
plan_sources.what_you_get: Footprint, height or stories, sometimes facade material, building type (masonry/wood/steel) and year built. No interior walls except where OSM indoor mapping exists.
plan_sources.limits: Exterior-only and often modeled; good for a desk estimate and donor-side planning, not for a design.

plan_sources.source: Field capture when no drawings exist
plan_sources.what_you_get: A scaled sketch or scan built on site.
plan_sources.how: Ranplan can build a 3D model from background images (Intelligent Floor Plan Recognition) or import IFC from the Metaroom LiDAR app; iBwave can create, scale and geolocate floor plans on its mobile planner.
plan_sources.limits: Wall materials still have to be identified by eye.

plan_request.subject: Request for building drawings - in-building public safety radio (ERCES/BDA) design at [Building name, address]
plan_request.body:
Hello [Name],

[Company] has been engaged to evaluate emergency responder radio coverage at [Building name, address] and, if needed, design an Emergency Responder Communication Enhancement System (ERCES/BDA) for fire code compliance. To model coverage and prepare the permit submittal the fire department requires, we need the drawings listed below. Electronic files are best: full-size vector PDFs of the sheets, plus DWG backgrounds or the Revit/IFC model if the architect can release them.

1. Architectural floor plans for every level, including basements, parking, mechanical penthouse and roof.
2. Reflected ceiling plans.
3. Building sections and exterior elevations for all sides.
4. Wall type / partition schedule and details, and the window/glazing schedule (including any low-E or coated glass).
5. Life safety (code) plans showing rated walls, shafts, stairs and the fire command center.
6. Electrical and fire alarm riser diagrams and the locations of electrical and telecom rooms.
7. Roof plan and site plan.
8. Structural floor type (concrete slab, metal deck with concrete fill, post-tensioned slab).
9. Any existing BDA/DAS as-built drawings or radio coverage test reports.

We will use the drawings only for the design, permitting and maintenance of this system and will not distribute them. If the architect needs your written authorization to release CAD files, a short email from you to them copying me is enough to start that.

If any items are not available, please tell me which, and we will work from what exists and field-verify the rest.

Thank you,
[Name]
[Title, company]
[Phone] | [Email]
ask_for: Architectural floor plans for ALL levels incl. roof, basements, parking (vector PDF at full sheet size; DWG if available) - AHJs require floor plans for every level, including levels without system components.
Reflected ceiling plans - antenna mounting surface and ceiling type for each area.
Building sections and exterior elevations for all exposures - floor-to-floor heights and facade composition; OCSD requires exterior elevations for all exposures.
Wall type / partition schedule and details - material of each wall for attenuation; Santa Clara County FD requires partitions, non-rated and rated walls on the ERRC floor plan.
Window/glazing schedule or spec (low-E, metallised or laminated glass) - coated glass can add tens of dB of loss.
Life safety / code plans - rated walls, shafts, stairs, fire command center, occupancy and construction type (SDFD cover sheet requires construction type per floor and occupancy classification).
Electrical and fire alarm riser diagrams, electrical/IDF room locations - power, monitoring tie-in and cable pathways; Fairfax requires the riser and firestop systems on the building permit plans.
Roof plan and site plan - donor antenna location and donor path; multi-building site map.
Structural floor/slab type - floor penetration loss.
Existing ERCES/BDA as-built drawings and test reports, if any.
Owner's written authorization for the architect/GC to release CAD/BIM files.

plan_formats.format: PDF (vector or scanned), Architectural D (24x36 in)
plan_formats.import_note: iBwave Design imports .pdf floor plans. Set scale from a graduated bar scale or a long known dimension: SDFD and OCSD require a graduated ruler on plan sheets, and OCSD says a relational scale such as 1"=20' is not acceptable. Santa Clara County FD sets 1/8"=1'-0" as the minimum ERRC plan scale.
iBwave Design imports .dwg and .dxf and exports projects to .dxf. Ranplan 'Smart CAD Extract' converts 2D/3D CAD files into 3D building models.

plan_formats.format: Raster images (JPEG, BMP, TIFF, GIF, photos of posted evacuation plans)
plan_formats.import_note: iBwave imports .jpeg, .bmp, .tiff and .gif and can create, scale and geolocate floor plans. Ranplan Intelligent Floor Plan Recognition converts background images into 3D vector building models.

plan_formats.format: IFC (open BIM exchange; exported from Revit, ArchiCAD, SketchUp, Tekla, etc.)
plan_formats.used_by: Architects using BIM; LiDAR scan apps
plan_formats.import_note: Ranplan Professional 6.9+ imports IFC with geometry, material properties and spatial relationships, and imports IFC from the Metaroom LiDAR app. The iBwave sources opened do not list IFC import.
No native .rvt import is stated in the Ranplan or iBwave sources opened; Ranplan names Revit as an IFC source, so request an IFC export.

Sheet ID = discipline + sheet type + sequence. Disciplines: A Architectural, S Structural, F Fire Protection, E Electrical, T Telecommunications. Sheet types: 1 plans, 2 elevations, 3 sections, 4 large-scale views, 5 details, 6 schedules and diagrams. So A-1xx are architectural plans and E-6xx usually holds riser diagrams/schedules.

open_data.name: OpenStreetMap buildings and indoor tags
open_data.what: Footprints with building=*, building:levels (above-ground levels, roof and underground excluded), height (m, ground to top of roof), building:material (outer facade surface material: brick, concrete, glass, metal, wood, plaster, cement_block, ...), roof:material; indoor=room/area/wall/corridor/door with level=* (Simple Indoor Tagging).
open_data.coverage: Global, crowd-sourced; attribute completeness varies building to building.
open_data.access: Overpass API (public instance https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter; keep under 10,000 queries and 1 GB per day for one-off use, divide by 100 for regular use, commercial users run their own server) or planet/extract files.

open_data.name: Microsoft GlobalMLBuildingFootprints
open_data.what: ML-derived footprints from Bing imagery with per-polygon height estimate (m; -1 if none) and confidence.
open_data.coverage: Global including the US (US refresh released 2022; new US data added July 2026).
open_data.access: dataset-links.csv lists files partitioned by country and level-9 quadkey; line-delimited GeoJSON (.csv.gz), EPSG:4326; also on Planetary Computer.

open_data.name: Google Open Buildings (v3)
open_data.what: ML footprints with area_in_meters, confidence, Plus Code; no building type or address.
open_data.coverage: Africa, South/South-East Asia, Latin America and Caribbean; mainland US not covered (Puerto Rico and USVI listed).
open_data.access: gs://open-buildings-data/v3/polygons_s2_level_4_gzip (CSV per S2 cell), Earth Engine asset.

open_data.name: Overture Maps buildings theme
open_data.what: Conflated footprints (OSM first, then Esri Community Maps, Microsoft, Google, others) with optional height, num_floors, num_floors_underground, min_height, facade_material, roof_material, roof_shape, class, subtype.
open_data.access: GeoParquet in cloud storage, e.g. s3://overturemaps-us-west-2/release/2026-10-21.0/theme=buildings/type=building/* (Azure mirror also).

open_data.name: FEMA/ORNL USA Structures
open_data.what: Footprints of structures larger than 450 sq ft with occupancy class (OCC_CLS), primary occupancy (PRIM_OCC), HEIGHT (m, only where NGA LiDAR covered 133 cities), SQMETERS, address, source, image date. No construction material or story count.
open_data.coverage: US and territories, about 127 million structures.
open_data.access: Figshare (DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.c.6895333.v1), FEMA Geospatial Resource Center (https://disasters.geoplatform.gov/USA_Structures/), Esri Living Atlas.

open_data.name: USACE National Structure Inventory (NSI) 2026
open_data.what: Modeled point inventory: bldgtype (M masonry, W wood, H manufactured, S steel), num_story, sqft, found_type, occtype, med_yr_blt (Census-tract median, not the building's own year), bldheight (m, public in 2026).
open_data.coverage: Nationwide US; many values modeled from parcel, footprint and HAZUS data.
open_data.access: API https://nsi.sec.usace.army.mil/nsiapi/structures?bbox=... or ?fips=..., GeoJSON; state GeoPackage/GeoParquet downloads.

open_data.name: County assessor improvement data (example: Cook County IL)
open_data.what: Building-level characteristics: year built, building sq ft, type of residence (stories), exterior wall material, roof material, basement.
open_data.coverage: County by county; the Cook County dataset covers residential single and multi-family (fewer than 7 units) only.

open_data.name: Regrid parcels
open_data.what: Parcel boundaries plus county-sourced yearbuilt, numstories, structstyle, area_building; Premium adds ll_bldg_count and ll_bldg_footprint_sqft.
open_data.coverage: 160M+ US parcels; attribute coverage varies by county.
open_data.access: Property app, API, data store, enterprise delivery.
open_data.cost: Commercial; the pricing page opened shows plans and enterprise sales but no published prices.

open_data.name: ATTOM property data
open_data.what: Assessor-derived characteristics: construction (material of the main structure), exterior wall material, roof cover and roof framing, building fire resistance class, levels, year built.
open_data.coverage: About 150 million US property records; accuracy depends on each assessor.
open_data.access: REST API (free API key / start-up plan offered) and ATTOM Cloud bulk tables.
open_data.cost: Commercial; free trial key; enterprise pricing not published.

ahj_plan_rules.ahj: San Diego Fire-Rescue (City of San Diego), Standard C-1
ahj_plan_rules.requirement: Fire permit required for every ERCES. Design and as-built submittals in PDF, Architectural D (24x36) landscape, all pages one size. Floor plans, exterior elevations and area drawings must carry a legend, a graduated-ruler scale, compass orientation and unique IDs. Cover sheet must state construction type per floor, floors above/below grade, square footage, occupancy and sprinkler standard. Floor plans for every level from roof to lowest level, including levels the system does not cover, with fire-rated protection callouts; system elevation schematic; donor path plan and elevation; 700 and 800 MHz link budgets. Test reports show each floor as 20 approximately equal grids. As-built plans and a final acceptance test report are due before TCO.

ahj_plan_rules.ahj: Orange County Sheriff's Department (Orange County, CA countywide 800 MHz system), Rev 4.5
ahj_plan_rules.requirement: Design submitted to a project portal; based at minimum on Architectural D (36x24) building prints in PDF. Must include building description (floors above/below grade, type of construction), riser with uplink/downlink power at all junctions, floor plans for all floors (including those without BDA components), exterior elevations for all exposures, and heat maps with the 20-grid method for every floor. Scale must be a graduated ruler; a relational scale such as 1"=20' is not accepted.

ahj_plan_rules.ahj: Santa Clara County Fire Department, SD&S C-2
ahj_plan_rules.requirement: Plans: title sheet, equipment list, SOP, floor plan, riser (single-line) diagram, secondary power calculations. Title sheet lists occupancy group, basements, stories, building height, total area and construction type. Floor plan shows the scale with a graphic scale (minimum 1/8"=1'-0"; metric not accepted), room names, and the locations of partitions, non-rated walls and rated walls.

ahj_plan_rules.ahj: Fairfax County, VA (DIT Radio Services Center + Land Development Services + Fire Marshal)
ahj_plan_rules.requirement: DIT reviews plans and technical specifications first. Building permit plans must show the extent of the system, the DIT-approved preliminary riser and all through-penetration firestop systems. The FCOMM permit needs the approved building plan pages showing communication-system items; full systems also need a fire alarm permit showing the ERCES-to-fire-alarm connection.

ERRC requests go to the City-County Inspections site. County fire protection submittals require shop drawings, life safety plans and an Appendix B, sealed by an NC-licensed PE or licensed fire sprinkler contractor, each document as its own file. (The City of Durham ERRCS guideline and permit-requirement PDFs returned HTTP 403 and were not read.)

formulas.name: P.2040 material model
formulas.formula: eps_r' = a*f^b ; sigma = c*f^d [S/m] ; eps_r'' = 17.98*sigma/f ; eps_rc = eps_r' - j*eps_r''  (f in GHz)
formulas.explain: Builds the complex relative permittivity of a material from Table 3 coefficients (eqs 57, 58, 59). Use the row whose frequency range covers your band; ranges are indicative, not hard limits, except for the ground types (1-10 GHz only).

formulas.name: P.2040 attenuation rate inside a material
formulas.formula: A_dielectric = 1636*sigma/sqrt(eps_r')  [dB/m] (valid for loss tangent < 0.5) ; A_conductor = 545.8*sqrt(sigma*f_GHz) [dB/m] (loss tangent > 15)
formulas.explain: Eqs (27a), (27b). Multiply by thickness for absorption only; reflections at the faces are extra.

formulas.name: P.2040 single-slab transmission, normal incidence (one-wall loss)
formulas.formula: R' = (1 - sqrt(eps_rc)) / (1 + sqrt(eps_rc)) ; q = (2*pi*d/lambda)*sqrt(eps_rc) ; T = (1 - R'^2)*exp(-j*q) / (1 - R'^2*exp(-j*2q)) ; Loss_dB = -20*log10(|T|)
formulas.explain: Eqs (43b), (44) with (37a) at theta = 0 (TE and TM coincide). d = thickness (m), lambda = free-space wavelength (m). For oblique incidence use (37a)/(37b) and q = (2*pi*d/lambda)*sqrt(eps_rc - sin^2(theta)). Reproduces P.2040-4 Fig 6 (about 7.5 dB for 0.2 m concrete at 1 GHz).

formulas.name: P.2040 multilayer wall (ABCD)
formulas.formula: Per layer m: A=D=cos(beta_m*d_m), B=j*Z_m*sin(beta_m*d_m), C=j*sin(beta_m*d_m)/Z_m, beta_m=k0*sqrt(eta_m) (normal incidence), Z_m=120*pi/sqrt(eta_m); multiply layer matrices; T = 2/(2A + B/Z0 + C*Z0), Z0 = 120*pi
formulas.explain: Attachment 1 to Annex 1, eqs (60)-(63). Model drywall-air-drywall, brick-air-sheathing, double glazing; air layers use eta = 1.

formulas.name: Thick-slab shortcut (derived)
formulas.explain: Derived by us from eq (43b) when the slab is lossy enough that the internal multiple-reflection term is negligible; not printed in P.2040. Use the full formula for thin or low-loss layers, where resonance can make loss swing by several dB.

formulas.name: 3GPP O2I building penetration
formulas.formula: PL = PL_b + PL_tw + PL_in + N(0, sigma_P^2) ; PL_tw = PL_npi - 10*log10( sum p_i*10^(-L_i/10) ) ; L_i = a_i + b_i*f (GHz)
formulas.explain: TR 38.901 eqs (7.4-2), (7.4-3), Tables 7.4.3-1/-2. Defined for 0.5-100 GHz; not for VHF/UHF below 500 MHz.

formulas.name: ITU-R P.2109 building entry loss
formulas.formula: L(P) = 10*log(10^(0.1*A) + 10^(0.1*B) + 10^(0.1*C)) ; A = F^-1(P)*sigma1 + mu1 ; B = F^-1(P)*sigma2 + mu2 ; C = -3 ; mu1 = Lh + Le ; Lh = r + s*log(f) + t*(log f)^2 ; Le = 0.212*|theta| ; mu2 = w + x*log(f) ; sigma1 = u + v*log(f) ; sigma2 = y + z*log(f)
formulas.explain: f in GHz, theta = elevation at the facade (deg), P = probability not exceeded. Table 1: traditional r=12.64 s=3.72 t=0.96 u=9.6 v=2.0 w=9.1 x=-3.0 y=4.5 z=-2.0; thermally-efficient r=28.19 s=-3.00 t=8.48 u=13.5 v=3.8 w=27.8 x=-2.9 y=9.4 z=-2.1. Valid about 80 MHz-100 GHz; not site-specific. 'log' read as log10 (ITU convention).

formulas.name: ITU-R P.1238 indoor site-general loss with floors
formulas.formula: L_total = L(d0) + N*log10(d/d0) + Lf(n) ; L(d0) = 20*log10(f_MHz) - 28 at d0 = 1 m
formulas.explain: Eq (2) of P.1238-13; Lf from Table 5 (e.g. office at 0.9 GHz: 9/19/24 dB for 1/2/3 floors), Lf = 0 when n = 0.

formulas.name: NISTIR 6055 regression curves
formulas.formula: Received signal magnitude (dB re free space) = M0 + M1*F + M2*F^2 + ... + M6*F^6, F in GHz
formulas.explain: Coefficients per specimen in Tables 4.xb (0.5-2 GHz) and 4.xd (3-8 GHz). Loss = minus the value. Do not evaluate outside the measured band.

formulas.name: Field-ratio to dB
formulas.explain: Used to convert the Cardinal %T (field-strength ratio EI/EO) to dB.
